subject: OrchardPay: Request for proportional remedy after short connect-failure spike
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@orchardpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: OrchardPay Support <support@orchardpay.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 22:03:12 +0000
Subject: Payment gateway spike — impact window and credits

Hi Soojin,

We saw a short but painful spike yesterday evening (US-PDT) where our checkout flow started returning 502/504 and elevated 429s for roughly five minutes. That window impacted a 10-minute customer-facing payment batch and caused several failed transactions that needed manual retry.

Summary:
- Window: 2028-09-11 21:57:40 - 22:03:10 UTC
- Symptoms: sudden 502/504 responses, 429 rate increase on /v1/payments, increased latency from ~180ms to ~3s
- Business impact: ~120 failed authorizations; our SREs had to roll back a client-side retry change to stabilize flows

Per our contract (SLA section 4.2), we believe this meets the threshold for a proportional remedy. Can you confirm Redwood's view on eligibility and the next steps for evidence and payout timing? We can attach traces and raw logs — I've pulled a trace bundle and gateway logs and can share immediately.

We'd also appreciate an expedited postmortem and a clear remediation plan.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Integrations, OrchardPay
elena@orchardpay.com

On Mon, Sep 11, 2028 at 22:03 Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 01:16:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment gateway spike — impact window and credits

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Elena — sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as an incident and will prioritize verification and remediation. Two quick asks so we can move fast:

1) Can you confirm the exact timezone for the timestamps you supplied (you listed UTC; that matches our logs but confirm if they were local times)
2) Please attach the trace bundle and gateway logs (ndjson or gz preferred). If you have a short list of example request IDs that failed, include those — they speed up correlation.

Next steps from our side: I've looped in Laura (serving/runtime) and Ben (SLO adjudication). Laura, Ben — can you kick off an initial impact check against US-West-2 serving pools and let us know whether this looks like a routing/fallback issue or an autoscaler churn? We'll aim to confirm eligibility for a remedy within 48 hours pending evidence.

Elena — we'll also confirm whether an expedited postmortem is possible within 5 business days and the typical credit payout cadence if this is adjudicated as eligible.

Sooj (on behalf of Customer Escalations)
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@orchardpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 10:11:07 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment gateway spike — impact window and credits

Hi Elena — I pulled the artifacts and correlated them with our serving logs for US-West-2. Preliminary findings:

- We see an autoscaler eviction event in the serving-overseer logs at 2028-09-11T21:58:05Z which triggered a rapid pod churn on a small subset of the pool handling OrchardPay's pinned model variant.
- The eviction caused transient rendezvous failures in the request router; initial reconnect attempts generated 502/504s, and the retry throttling on the client-side generated the 429 surge you saw.
- Measured high-latency tail: mean latency rose from 180ms to 2.8s for affected tokens in that 5–6 minute window; consistent with your traces.

Given the eviction and missed fallback routing (we failed to reroute to cold-standby replicas fast enough), this appears eligible under SLA Section 4.2. We will run the adjudication checklist (validate ownership of request IDs, confirm lack of client misconfiguration, and confirm the measured availability delta).

Proposed next steps:
1) Adjudication owner: Ben (SLO team) — Ben, please confirm whether this meets the credit threshold and estimate the prorated credit amount.
2) Remediation: we'll treat this as a priority fix for the autoscaler policy and will propose a canary rollout with an updated autoscale aggressiveness profile.
3) Postmortem: target draft by 2028-09-17 COB, internal review 09-18, shareable PM summary 09-19. If OrchardPay needs it earlier, we'll escalate.

Evidence we included in the adjudication bundle: the traces you supplied, routing logs, and the autoscaler event trace.

Laura Bennett
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Quick adjudication note: I validated the request IDs against our ingest. Ownership confirmed, client retries do not indicate misconfiguration, and the measured availability drop exceeds the 0.5% monthly SLA threshold when prorated over the 30-day period.

Estimated prorated credit: 0.18% of September's invoice (preliminary) — final calculation pending Marcus for finance/payout timing.

Marcus — can you confirm the expected timeline for issuing a credit once adjudicated and whether we need a formal acceptance signature from OrchardPay?

Ben Carter
SLO & Reliability, Redwood Inference

Thanks, all — and thanks for the artifacts, Elena.

Finance/process notes: once Ben finalizes the adjudication number (0.18% preliminary), we run a single-line credit against the September invoice. Typical timeline: credit issued on next billing run (within 7–10 business days) after we receive a confirmation e-mail from the customer accepting the credit and a short support form we send (not DocuSign).

Action items for OrchardPay: please reply to this thread with a short acceptance line like "OrchardPay accepts Redwood's proposed credit of X% against the September invoice" and confirm an account contact for payout.
